builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
summary: The method replaces human teleoperation for collecting robot demonstration data with a coding agent that rebuilds the task in simulation, generates expert actions, and renders photorealistic videos via a video model, charging roughly $21 per task setup plus $0.80 per episode. Costs are API usage, a $5 render contract, and dependence on an external simulator, video model, and judge ensemble rather than on local GPU or cluster resources. It can fail if the simulator, video model, or judges are unavailable or too expensive, if the reconstructed scene or controller does not match real dynamics, or if judge certification passes low-quality episodes that degrade the trained policy.
rationale: It is relevant only to teams operating real robots and depends on external simulation, video-model, and judge infrastructure rather than on the reader's constrained GPU or API budget.

claims.statement: The method replaces human teleoperation for collecting robot demonstration data with a coding agent that rebuilds the task in simulation, generates expert actions, and renders photorealistic videos via a video model, charging roughly $21 per task setup plus $0.80 per episode. Costs are API usage, a $5 render contract, and dependence on an external simulator, video model, and judge ensemble rather than on local GPU or cluster resources. It can fail if the simulator, video model, or judges are unavailable or too expensive, if the reconstructed scene or controller does not match real dynamics, or if judge certification passes low-quality episodes that degrade the trained policy.

Farm-only policies match teleoperation-trained policies (93 vs. 84 successes in 100 trials) and retain 87 successes under unseen tablecloth and coloured light where teleoperation-trained policies fall to 46; one hour of three-view data costs $107 versus $117 teleoperation in China and $290 labour in North America.
